title: Longest Palindrome

content.problemStatement:
You're given a string of letters, treated as a bag of characters rather
than a fixed sequence: you may rearrange the letters however you like,
and you don't have to use all of them.

**Using some or all of the letters in the string, return the length of
the longest palindrome you can build.**

This is not about finding a palindromic substring inside `s`, it's
about what palindrome you could construct from its letters. The
comparison is case-sensitive, so 'a' and 'A' are different letters.
constraints: s consists of lowercase and/or uppercase English letters only
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: one longest palindrome buildable is "dccaccd", length 7 (the second 'd' or extra letters are left unused)
a single letter is trivially a palindrome of length 1
both letters match, so the whole string is used as "bb"

hints: Consider using a frequency map, hash table, or fixed-size array of 26/128 elements to track character counts.
If searching for substrings or window constraints, the sliding window technique with two pointers is often optimal.
Watch out for edge cases such as empty strings, single-character strings, and differing cases.
learningObjectives: Master core algorithmic concepts and pattern recognition for Longest Palindrome.
Analyze time and space complexity trade-offs to meet optimal constraint benchmarks.
Formulate robust solutions addressing edge cases including boundary values and empty sets.
